mainTopic: The reward for waiting after תפילה, the hidden מזיקין, the שכינה among those who pray, judge and learn, and ה׳'s תפילין
overview: This amud opens with רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's answer to the question at the end of the previous amud: one who waits for his friend in שול after תפילה earns the blessings of a פסוק in ישעיה. The גמרא then describes the countless unseen מזיקין around every person, quoting אבא בנימין, אביי, רב הונא and רבא. It explains how one could detect or even see them, and tells how רב ביבי בר אביי tried it and was harmed. Next, אבא בנימין teaches that תפלה is fully heard in the בית הכנסת, and רבי יצחק adds that the שכינה is with ten who pray, three who judge, two who learn, and even one who learns. The גמרא asks why each larger group is needed and finds something special in each, including רב אשי's teaching that a מצוה one planned but was prevented from doing counts as done. Finally, רבי יצחק teaches that ה׳ wears תפילין‎. ה׳'s תפילין contain praises of ישראל, just as ours contain praises of ה׳, and the גמרא works out how those praises fit into the four compartments.

steps.title: The reward for waiting for a friend after praying
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says that one who waits for his friend to finish praying earns the blessings in a פסוק from ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: He earns these blessings, as it says: 'If only you had listened to My commandments, your peace would be like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea. Your descendants would be like the sand, and the children of your body…'
steps.whatsHappening: The previous lines (on the previous amud) asked what the reward is for someone who waits for his friend in שול. Here רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers: he earns the blessings of this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about one who 'listens to My מצוות.' The מפרשים connect the word מצוה to צוותא, meaning 'company,' so keeping your friend company counts as this kind of listening. The reward is peace, righteousness, and many children.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק)
the children of your body, your descendants
'and so on,' meaning the פסוק continues

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'these blessings' point forward to the blessings in the פסוק. They do not point back to something listed earlier. The question this answers ('what is his reward?') appears on the previous amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that staying with a friend so he is not left alone is treated as a real מצוה with a big reward.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
He merits these blessings,
phrases.notes: Refers to the one who waits for his friend to finish praying.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'If only you had listened to My commandments,'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 48:18. מצוה is read in the sense of צוותא, 'company.'

phrases.english: your peace would be like a river,
and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your descendants would be like the sand,
and the offspring of your body…' and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: זוֹכֶה לַבְּרָכוֹת הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the previous amud: what is the reward for one who waits for his friend?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who waits for his friend after תפילה earns the blessings of peace, righteousness, and many descendants listed in ישעיה 48:18–19.

steps.title: If we could see the demons, no one could survive
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא בנימין: if our eyes could see the מזיקין, nobody could bear it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: אבא בנימין says: If the eye were allowed to see, no creature could stand up against the harmful spirits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that opens a new but related topic: the huge number of invisible מזיקין around us. This helps explain why leaving a friend alone is dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא בנימין says the only reason people can live calmly is that the מזיקין are hidden from sight. If we could see them, the sight alone would overwhelm any person. This sets up the next two statements, which describe just how many there are.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
if only / were it the case that

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Binyamin says:
If permission were given
to the eye to see —
no creature would be able
to stand up before the demons.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא בִּנְיָמִין אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reward for waiting to the danger behind it: the unseen מזיקין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מזיקין are everywhere. Only the fact that we cannot see them lets people live normally.

steps.title: אביי: they surround us like dirt around a pit
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the מזיקין outnumber us and surround us like the dirt piled around a ditch.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They are more numerous than we are, and they stand around us like the mound of earth around a pit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues אבא בנימין's idea. He gives a picture of how many מזיקין there are and how close they stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Think of a pit that has just been dug. The dirt piles up on every side, right at its edge. אביי says the מזיקין crowd around a person in the same way: more of them than people, and pressed close on all sides.

phrases.english: Abaye said: They are more numerous than us,
and they stand around us
like the earth mound around a pit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִינְהוּ נְפִישִׁי מִינַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands אבא בנימין's statement by describing how many מזיקין there are and how close they are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזיקין outnumber people and surround them on all sides.

steps.title: רב הונא: a thousand on the left, ten thousand on the right
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא gives a number: every person has 1,000 מזיקין on his left and 10,000 on his right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Each and every one of us has a thousand on his left and ten thousand on his right.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes this short series by putting a number on the מזיקין around each person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His numbers come from תהלים 91:7: 'A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand; they will not come near you.' The point is twofold. The danger is enormous, and only הקב״ה's protection keeps a person safe.
steps.whatToRemember: The reward for waiting for a friend after תפילה is great. The background is that every person is surrounded by countless unseen מזיקין: 1,000 on the left and 10,000 on the right according to רב הונא. Being left alone can be dangerous.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the גמרא treats leaving a friend alone in שול so seriously. The danger is real, so keeping him company is a real kindness.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כֹּל חַד וְחַד מִינַּן,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: Each and every one of us
has a thousand on his left
phrases.notes: Based on תהלים 91:7, 'יִפֹּל מִצִּדְּךָ אֶלֶף'.

phrases.english: and ten thousand on his right.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כֹּל חַד וְחַד מִינַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a specific number to the general idea from אבא בנימין and אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person is surrounded by 1,000 מזיקין on his left and 10,000 on his right.

steps.title: Everyday troubles that come from the demons
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists four common problems that are really caused by the מזיקין: crowding at the כלה, tired knees, worn-out clothes of the רבנן, and hurting feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The crowding at the כלה gatherings comes from the demons. Tired knees come from them. The clothes of the רבנן that wear out are worn down by rubbing against them. Feet that hurt come from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues the topic of מזיקין by naming four ordinary problems that they cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 2–4 said the מזיקין are many and are all around us. רבא now shows what that means in daily life. Things that seem to have no cause, such as a crowded room, knees that ache for no reason, and clothes wearing out even without hard work, are explained as the result of the crowds of מזיקין pushing and rubbing against us.

keyTerms.meaning: The large public Torah-learning gatherings held in אלול and אדר

steps.confusionAlert: The word כלה here does not mean a bride. It is the name of the big learning gatherings held twice a year.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This crowding that happens at the kalla gathering
comes from them (the demons).
phrases.notes: Even though the people present could fit, it feels packed because the demons take up space.

phrases.english: Those knees that feel tired
come from them.
Those clothes of the Sages that wear out
phrases.notes: Even though Torah scholars do not do hard physical work.

phrases.english: come from their rubbing against them.
Those feet that ache
come from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי דּוּחְקָא דְּהָוֵי בְּכַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the large numbers of מזיקין given by אביי and רב הונא, and shows their practical effects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crowding at the כלה, tired knees, worn clothing of scholars, and aching feet are all caused by the מזיקין.

steps.title: How to detect the demons and how to see them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives two methods. Spreading ash around the bed shows their footprints. A special powder made from a cat's afterbirth lets a person see them, and it must be stored carefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who wants to know the demons are there should spread fine ash around his bed. In the morning he will see marks like a rooster's footprints. Someone who wants to actually see them should take the afterbirth of a black female cat, born to a black female cat, a firstborn born to a firstborn. He should burn it, grind it, and put some in his eyes, and he will see them. Then he should put the rest in an iron tube and seal it with an iron seal, so they do not steal it from him, and he should seal its opening so that he is not harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the topic and explains two methods. The first only proves the מזיקין are there. The second lets a person actually see them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. Ash only shows signs that they were present, the bird-like footprints. The cat-afterbirth powder lets a person see them directly. The safety steps at the end, the iron tube, the iron seal, and closing it up, show that this is dangerous, and that sets up the warning story in the next step.

phrases.english: One who wants to know of them (that they exist)
should bring fine, sifted ash
and spread it around his bed,
and in the morning he will see marks like a rooster's footprints.
One who wants to see them
should bring the afterbirth of a black female cat
who is the daughter of a black female cat,
a firstborn who is the daughter of a firstborn,
and burn it in fire, and grind it,
and fill his eyes with it, and he will see them.
Then he should put the rest in an iron tube,
and seal it with an iron seal,
in case they (the demons) steal it from him,
and he should seal its opening,
phrases.notes: Sefaria understands פומיה as the opening of the tube. Some read it as sealing his own mouth, meaning he should not talk about what he saw.

phrases.english: so that he will not be harmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לְמִידַּע לְהוּ לַיְיתֵי קִיטְמָא נְהִילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of מזיקין. After describing what they do, the גמרא explains how a person can detect or see them. This connects back to אבא בנימין's point in step 2 that our eyes cannot see them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ash around the bed reveals the footprints of the מזיקין. The burnt and ground afterbirth of a firstborn black cat, born to a firstborn black cat, lets a person see them, but the powder must be sealed in iron for safety.

steps.title: רב ביבי בר אביי tried it and was harmed
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי used the method to see the מזיקין and was harmed. The רבנן prayed for him and he was healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי did this. He saw them and was harmed. The רבנן prayed for mercy for him, and he was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short true story about someone who actually used the method from the previous step. It went badly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story backs up the danger hinted at in step 6. Even a great scholar was hurt by seeing the מזיקין. This also connects to step 2: אבא בנימין said that if we could see them, we could not stand it. It is safest not to try. The story ends with the תפלה of the רבנן healing him, which leads smoothly into the next topic, the power of prayer.
steps.whatToRemember: The מזיקין section ends with a warning: seeing them is dangerous, as אבא בנימין said in step 2, and what saved רב ביבי was the תפלה of the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי עֲבַד הָכִי,
phrases.english: Rav Bivi bar Abaye did this;
he saw them and was harmed.
The Sages prayed for mercy for him,
and he was healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי עֲבַד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened when someone actually used the method from step 6, and closes the discussion of the מזיקין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the מזיקין is truly dangerous. רב ביבי בר אביי was harmed and was healed only through the prayers of the רבנן.

steps.title: Prayer is fully heard only in the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא בנימין: a person's תפלה is heard only in a בית הכנסת. He proves it from a פסוק that puts רנה (song) and תפלה together.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that אבא בנימין says: A person's prayer is heard only in the בית הכנסת, as the פסוק says, 'to listen to the song and to the prayer.' Where there is song, that is where prayer should be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of תפלה, which was the subject of step 1, with a new teaching from אבא בנימין about where to pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from שלמה's prayer at the dedication of the Temple, in מלכים א ח. That פסוק mentions רנה, song and praise, right next to תפלה. אבא בנימין reads this as a rule: prayer belongs in the place where the community sings praise to הקדוש ברוך הוא, which is the בית הכנסת. The point is not that private prayer is ignored. It means prayer is heard most fully and properly in the shul.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same אבא בנימין from step 2, but this is a separate teaching on a new topic, prayer, not demons.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is a main source for the importance of davening in a בית הכנסת. The next step builds on it.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Abba Binyamin says:
A person's prayer is not heard
except in the synagogue,
as it is said: 'To listen to the song and to the prayer' (I Kings 8:28).
phrases.notes: Said by שלמה המלך at the dedication of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: In the place of song (praise),
there prayer should be.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא בִּנְיָמִין אוֹמֵר: אֵין תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל אָדָם נִשְׁמַעַת אֶלָּא בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the long aside on מזיקין, which began with אבא בנימין in step 2, the גמרא brings another teaching of his and returns to the topic of תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's תפלה is fully heard only in the בית הכנסת, the place of communal רנה, based on the פסוק pairing רנה with תפלה.

steps.title: God is present in the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא, quoting רבי יצחק, brings a פסוק showing that הקדוש ברוך הוא is found in the בית הכנסת: 'God stands in the congregation of God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: How do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא is found in the בית הכנסת? Because the פסוק says: 'God stands in the congregation of God.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא brings a פסוק that supports and explains the previous step: God is right there in the shul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא בנימין said prayer is heard in the בית הכנסת. רבי יצחק gives the reason: הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself is present there. The 'congregation of God' in תהלים פב is understood as the community gathered to pray, and God 'stands' among them. So prayer said there is said right in His presence.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a series of teachings on the special presence of the שכינה among those who gather to pray and learn, and it gives the reasoning behind praying in a בית הכנסת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is present in the synagogue?
As it is said: 'God stands in the congregation of God' (Psalms 82:1).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָצוּי בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and explains אבא בנימין's teaching: prayer in the בית הכנסת is heard because הקדוש ברוך הוא is present there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא is present in the בית הכנסת, as learned from 'אלהים נצב בעדת אל.'

steps.title: Ten who pray have the שכינה with them
steps.stepSummary: The teaching continues. A group of ten who pray has the שכינה with them, learned from ״אֱלֹהִים נִצָּב בַּעֲדַת אֵל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that when ten people pray, the שכינה is with them? Because it says: 'God stands in the congregation (עדה) of God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues past the בית הכנסת. It says that any group of ten people praying has the שכינה with them. This opens a list of three groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק from step 9 is now used to teach a number. The word עֵדָה (congregation) means a group of at least ten people. So the פסוק is really saying that God stands among ten who pray. This is the first and biggest group in a list that keeps getting smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asks for a source in a פסוק)
Ten, the minimum for a מנין
Congregation, a group of at least ten

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same פסוק as step 9, but it is not a repeat. In step 9 it taught that God is found in the בית הכנסת. Here the focus is the word עדה, which means ten people.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the sources for the idea that praying with a מנין of ten brings the שכינה.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that ten who pray
have the Divine Presence with them?
As it says: 'God stands in the congregation of God.'
phrases.notes: A עדה (congregation) is at least ten people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לַעֲשָׂרָה שֶׁמִּתְפַּלְּלִין שֶׁשְּׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק as step 9 and adds the number ten, which comes from the word עדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten people praying together have the שכינה with them.

steps.title: Three who sit in judgment have the שכינה with them
steps.stepSummary: Three judges sitting in a court have the שכינה with them, learned from ״בְּקֶרֶב אֱלֹהִים יִשְׁפֹּט״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that when three sit in judgment, the שכינה is with them? Because it says: 'In the midst of the judges He judges.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list goes down one level. Three judges sitting as a בית דין also have the שכינה with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second half of the same פסוק in תהלים. Here אֱלֹהִים means 'judges,' not God. The smallest court is three judges, so the פסוק means God is present among three who judge.

keyTerms.meaning: Three, the minimum number of judges for a court

steps.confusionAlert: In ״בְּקֶרֶב אֱלֹהִים יִשְׁפֹּט״ the word אלהים means human judges. 'He judges' refers to God, who judges among them.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that three who sit in judgment
have the Divine Presence with them?
As it says: 'In the midst of the judges He judges.'
phrases.notes: The smallest court is three judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לִשְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין בַּדִּין שֶׁשְּׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes down the ladder from ten to three. It uses the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three judges sitting in a court have the שכינה with them.

steps.title: Two who learn Torah together have the שכינה with them
steps.stepSummary: Two people who sit and learn תורה together have the שכינה with them, learned from the פסוק in מלאכי ״אָז נִדְבְּרוּ יִרְאֵי ה׳״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that when two sit and learn תורה, the שכינה is with them? Because it says: 'Then those who feared ה׳ spoke one with another, and ה׳ listened,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The list goes down to two. Two people learning תורה together, like a חברותא, also have the שכינה with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'a man with his friend,' which means two people. It says they spoke about holy matters and ה׳ listened. The word וְגוֹ׳ ('and so on') tells us the rest of the פסוק is not quoted, and the next step asks about a phrase from that unquoted part.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with his friend (two people)
And so on: the rest of the פסוק is not quoted

phrases.english: And from where do we know that two who sit and learn Torah
have the Divine Presence with them?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אָז נִדְבְּרוּ יִרְאֵי ה׳ אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ
phrases.english: As it says: 'Then those who feared ה׳ spoke one with another,'
phrases.notes: From מלאכי ג:טז. 'One with another' means two people.

phrases.english: 'and ה׳ listened,' and so on.
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues: '...for those who fear ה׳ and who think of His name.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לִשְׁנַיִם שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין וְעוֹסְקִין בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁשְּׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes down the ladder from three to two and brings a new פסוק from מלאכי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people learning תורה together have the שכינה with them.

steps.title: What does 'those who think of His name' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase ״וּלְחֹשְׁבֵי שְׁמוֹ״ means. It comes from the end of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and for those who think of His name'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about a phrase in the rest of the פסוק from מלאכי. This step sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already mentions 'those who fear ה׳.' So what does 'those who think of His name' add? The question looks for a new meaning in the words 'thinking of' His name.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (asks for the meaning of a word or phrase)
And for those who think of His name

steps.confusionAlert: This phrase was not written out in step 12. It is hidden inside the וְגוֹ׳ ('and so on'). It is part of the same פסוק in מלאכי.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'and for those who think of His name'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וּלְחֹשְׁבֵי שְׁמוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the main point about two learners to explain another phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the extra phrase 'those who think of His name.'

steps.title: Planning a מצוה but being forced not to do it counts as doing it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains: if a person planned to do a מצוה and was forced by circumstances not to do it, the פסוק gives him credit as if he did it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If a person planned to do a מצוה, but something outside his control stopped him and he did not do it, the פסוק counts it for him as if he did it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from step 13. 'Thinking of His name' means planning to do a מצוה. Even if the person was stopped, he is written in ה׳'s 'book of remembrance' as if he did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists 'those who think' next to 'those who fear ה׳.' This shows that a real plan to do a מצוה is counted, even without the action. There is one condition: he must be נאנס, stopped by something outside his control, not by his own laziness.

keyTerms.meaning: He was forced, prevented by something outside his control (אונס)
The פסוק counts it for him

steps.whatToRemember: The ladder: ten who pray, three who judge, and two who learn all have the שכינה with them. Then רב אשי teaches that a person who truly planned a מצוה but was stopped by אונס gets credit as if he did it.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying that thinking alone is enough. The credit is for someone who meant to do the מצוה and was forced not to. It does not apply to someone who simply chose not to act.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the idea that a sincere plan to do a מצוה is rewarded when an אונס gets in the way.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
If a person planned to do a מצוה,
and was forced by circumstances, and did not do it,
the verse counts it for him as if he had done it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: חָשַׁב אָדָם לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Those who think of His name' are people who planned a מצוה but were stopped by אונס. The פסוק counts them as if they did it.

steps.title: Even one person learning תורה has the Divine Presence
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the list: even a single person who learns תורה has the שכינה with him, learned from a פסוק in שמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that even one person who sits and learns תורה has the שכינה with him? Because the פסוק says: "In every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the last and smallest group to the list: even one person alone who learns תורה has the שכינה with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list went from ten, to three, to two, and now goes down to one. The פסוק speaks to a single person ("I will come to you," in the singular). Mentioning God's Name here is understood as learning תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know? (asks for a source)
I will cause My Name to be mentioned

phrases.english: And from where do we know that even one
who sits and learns Torah
has the Divine Presence with him?
As it says: "In every place
phrases.notes: שמות כ:כא

phrases.english: where I cause My Name to be mentioned
I will come to you and bless you."
phrases.notes: "You" is singular, so it applies to one person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final, smallest group (one person) to the list that began in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even one person learning תורה has the שכינה with him.

steps.title: If one is enough, why mention two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the list: if even one person has the שכינה, why teach it separately about two?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since even one person has the שכינה, is it necessary to say it about two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what looks like an extra, unneeded line in the list. It is setting up an answer that will show what two people get beyond what one gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the smallest group already has the שכינה, every bigger group should obviously have it too. So the separate teaching about two looks pointless unless two people get something more.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it necessary? (implies it should be obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not doubting that two people have the שכינה. It asks why the teaching bothered to say so.

phrases.english: But since even one has it,
is it necessary to say two?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ חַד, תְּרֵי מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 15 to challenge the need for step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The separate teaching about two people learning together (step 12).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one person has the שכינה, two people certainly do, so the teaching about two looks extra.

steps.title: Two people's words are written in the Book of Remembrance
steps.stepSummary: Two people get something extra: their words of תורה are written in the ספר הזכרונות, but one person's are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: With two people, their words are written in the Book of Remembrance. With one person, his words are not written in the Book of Remembrance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two people get an extra reward: their תורה is recorded in God's ספר הזכרונות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both one and two have the שכינה, but they differ in one way. The פסוק in מלאכי used for two people says "וַיִּכָּתֵב סֵפֶר זִכָּרוֹן" ("a book of remembrance was written"). That writing is promised only to people who "spoke to one another," which needs at least two.

phrases.english: Two: their words are written
in the Book of Remembrance,
phrases.notes: From מלאכי ג:טז, the פסוק quoted in step 12.

phrases.english: one: his words are not written
in the Book of Remembrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי מִכַּתְבָן מִלַּיְיהוּ בְּסֵפֶר הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an extra benefit that only the larger group gets.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two people get nothing more than one, so the teaching about two is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two people also have their words written in the ספר הזכרונות, which one person does not.

steps.title: If two is enough, why mention three?
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge again: if two people have the שכינה, why teach it separately about three judges?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since even two people have the שכינה, is it necessary to say it about three?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same kind of challenge one level up. It is setting up an explanation of why three judges needed their own mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people already get the שכינה and the ספר הזכרונות, so three should be included automatically. That makes the teaching about three judges look extra.

phrases.english: But since even two have it,
is it necessary to say three?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ תְּרֵי, תְּלָתָא מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge of step 16 for the next group.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two have the שכינה, three should be included automatically.

steps.title: Judging a case also counts as תורה
steps.stepSummary: Without the teaching about three, we might think judging is just keeping the peace and brings no שכינה. The teaching shows that דין is also תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: judging is just a way to keep peace, and the שכינה does not come. So it teaches us that judging is also תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the teaching about three judges is not about the number at all. It teaches that judging a case counts as learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first guess (מהו דתימא) is that a court is only a practical tool for settling fights between people, not a holy activity. The teaching about three (קמשמע לן) shows that a בית דין ruling by the תורה's laws is doing תורה, so the שכינה comes.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken first thought)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic idea: a judge deciding a case by the הלכה is not doing mere civil work. He is engaged in תורה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
judging is merely for keeping peace,
and the Divine Presence does not come;
so it teaches us
that judging is also Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא דִּינָא שְׁלָמָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא / קמשמע לן: the teaching blocks a mistaken idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Judging is only for social peace, so the שכינה does not come.
steps.terutzMaskana: Judging is also תורה, so the שכינה comes to the judges.

steps.title: If three is enough, why mention ten?
steps.stepSummary: The last round of the challenge: if three have the שכינה, why teach it separately about ten who pray?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since even three have the שכינה, is it necessary to say it about ten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same challenge one last time, about the group of ten. It is setting up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If three already have the שכינה, a group of ten should be included automatically. So the teaching about ten (step 10) looks extra.

phrases.english: But since even three have it,
is it necessary to say ten?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ תְּלָתָא, עֲשָׂרָה מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge pattern for the largest group.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching about ten who pray (step 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If three have the שכינה, ten should be included automatically.

steps.title: With ten, the Divine Presence arrives first
steps.stepSummary: With ten, the שכינה is already there before they gather. With three judges, it comes only once they sit down to judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: With ten, the שכינה comes first and is there before them. With three, it comes only when they sit down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ten get something extra: the שכינה is already waiting for them, even before they begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק for ten says God "נִצָּב" (stands) in the congregation, as if already there when they arrive. The פסוק for three says "בְּקֶרֶב אֱלֹהִים יִשְׁפֹּט," meaning God joins them only once they are actually judging. So ten is not extra: it shows the שכינה comes ahead of time.
steps.whatToRemember: Each group in the list gets something special. One person: the שכינה. Two people: their words are written in the ספר הזכרונות. Three judges: judging counts as תורה. Ten: the שכינה arrives even before they gather.

phrases.english: Ten: the Divine Presence comes ahead of them.
phrases.notes: Based on "אֱלֹהִים נִצָּב בַּעֲדַת אֵל" from step 10.

phrases.english: Three: only once they sit down.
phrases.notes: Based on "בְּקֶרֶב אֱלֹהִים יִשְׁפֹּט" from step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂרָה קָדְמָה שְׁכִינָה וְאָתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 and closes the series of challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a difference in timing between the groups.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ten get nothing more than three, so the teaching about ten is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: With ten the שכינה is there before them. With three it comes only once they sit to judge.

steps.title: ה׳ wears תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא wears תפילין. His source is the פסוק‎ 'ה׳ swore by His right hand and by the arm of His strength.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: How do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא wears תפילין? Because the פסוק says, 'ה׳ swore by His right hand and by the arm of His strength.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new אגדה. רבי יצחק says that ה׳ wears תפילין and gives a פסוק as the source. The next step will explain how the פסוק shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person swears while holding something holy. So when the פסוק says ה׳ swore 'by His right hand' and 'by the arm of His strength,' those must be holy objects. Right now we only have the claim and the פסוק. The decoding of the פסוק comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? The opening of a request for a source.
The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה׳)

steps.confusionAlert: This is אגדה describing ה׳ in human-like terms. The point is the deep connection between ה׳ and ישראל. Do not read it as saying ה׳ has a body.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda said,
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
wears tefillin?
As it says: 'ה׳ swore by His right hand
phrases.notes: ישעיהו סב:ח

phrases.english: and by the arm of His strength.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה by רבי יצחק, following the earlier teachings about ה׳'s closeness to people who learn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ wears תפילין, as shown by the פסוק 'נשבע ה׳ בימינו ובזרוע עזו.'

steps.title: Decoding right hand and arm of strength
steps.stepSummary: 'His right hand' means תורה, based on 'מימינו אש דת למו.' 'The arm of His strength' means תפילין, based on 'ה׳ עז לעמו יתן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His right hand' means the תורה, as it says, 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them.' 'The arm of His strength' means תפילין, as it says, 'ה׳ will give strength to His people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each part of the פסוק from the last step, using other פסוקים to show what each word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each key word is matched to another פסוק that uses the same word. 'Right hand' appears with the giving of the תורה, so it means תורה. 'Strength' (עז) is linked to ה׳ giving strength to His people, and that strength is תפילין. So ה׳ swore by תורה and by תפילין.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof that 'strength' means תפילין is not finished here. The next steps show why תפילין count as 'strength' for ישראל.

phrases.english: 'By His right hand' refers to the Torah,
as it says: 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them,'
phrases.notes: דברים לג:ב

phrases.english: 'And by the arm of His strength' refers to tefillin,
as it says: 'ה׳ will give strength to His people.'
phrases.notes: תהלים כט:יא

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימִינוֹ זוֹ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'right hand' and 'arm of strength' in ה׳'s oath are תורה and תפילין
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים לג:ב (מימינו אש דת למו) and תהלים כט:יא (ה׳ עז לעמו יתן)

steps.title: Why are תפילין called strength
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that תפילין are 'strength' for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that תפילין are strength for ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the last step. It wants proof that 'strength' really means תפילין. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said 'ה׳ will give strength to His people' refers to תפילין, but the פסוק never says the word תפילין. So the גמרא needs a separate source that links תפילין to strength. This is a request for more information, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where? A follow-up request for a source.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that tefillin are strength for Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁהַתְּפִילִּין עוֹז הֵם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for support for the claim in step 23 that 'strength' means תפילין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that תפילין give strength to ישראל

steps.title: The nations will see and fear
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק: 'All the nations of the land will see that ה׳'s name is called upon you, and they will fear you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And all the nations of the land will see that the name of ה׳ is called upon you, and they will be afraid of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a פסוק that describes the nations fearing ישראל because ה׳'s name is on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being feared by the nations is a kind of strength. The פסוק says this fear comes from 'ה׳'s name being called upon you.' The next step explains that this 'name' means תפילין, which finishes the link between תפילין and strength.

keyTerms.meaning: ה׳'s name is called upon you

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And all the nations of the land will see
phrases.notes: דברים כח:י

phrases.english: that the name of ה׳ is called upon you,
and they will be afraid of you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וְרָאוּ כׇּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says the nations will fear ישראל because ה׳'s name is upon them, which is a form of strength.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the head תפילין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי אליעזר הגדול explained 'ה׳'s name is called upon you' as the תפילין of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר הגדול says, this means the תפילין of the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the פסוק it just quoted is talking about תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר הגדול says 'ה׳'s name upon you' means the תפילין worn on the head. Now the chain is complete: head תפילין carry ה׳'s name, the nations fear ישראל because of it, and that fear is 'strength.' This confirms that 'the arm of His strength' in step 23 means תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The great רבי אליעזר (רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס)
The תפילין worn on the head

steps.whatToRemember: The full chain: 'the arm of His strength' means 'strength,' strength means תפילין, because the nations fear ישראל when they see ה׳'s name on them in the head תפילין.

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
This refers to the tefillin of the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַגָּדוֹל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 25 by showing that its פסוק refers to תפילין.
steps.raayaObject: That 'ה׳'s name is called upon you' refers to תפילין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אליעזר הגדול

steps.title: What is written in ה׳'s תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רב חייא בר אבין what is written in the תפילין of the Master of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רב חייא בר אבין: These תפילין of the Master of the world, what is written in them?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the idea that ה׳ wears תפילין, an אמורא asks what is inside them. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תפילין contain פסוקים about ה׳, like שמע ישראל. So it makes sense to ask what ה׳'s תפילין contain. The question sets up an answer about ה׳'s love for ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said
to Rav Chiya bar Avin:
These tefillin of the Master of the world,
what is written in them?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תְּפִילִּין דְּמָרֵי עָלְמָא מָה כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 22's teaching that ה׳ wears תפילין.

steps.title: Who is like Your people Israel
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין answers that ה׳'s תפילין contain 'Who is like Your people ישראל, one nation in the land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'And who is like Your people ישראל, one nation in the land?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין answers that ה׳'s תפילין contain a פסוק praising ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תפילין praise ה׳'s oneness (שמע ישראל ה׳ אחד), and ה׳'s תפילין praise ישראל's uniqueness ('one nation'). The bond goes both ways. ישראל declares ה׳ is one, and ה׳ declares ישראל is one special nation.

keyTerms.meaning: And who is like Your people?

steps.whatToRemember: ה׳'s תפילין mirror ours. We praise ה׳ as One, and ה׳ praises ישראל as one unique nation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This אגדה is the root of the well-known idea of mutual love between ה׳ and ישראל, which the גמרא continues to develop.

phrases.english: He said to him:
'And who is like Your people Israel,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א יז:כא

phrases.english: one nation in the land?'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ וּמִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳'s תפילין contain the פסוק 'ומי כעמך ישראל גוי אחד בארץ.'

steps.title: Is ה׳ praised through the praise of Israel?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק follows up: is הקדוש ברוך הוא really glorified through the praise of ישראל?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is the Holy One, Blessed be He, really praised through the praises of ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק follows up on the last answer. ה׳'s תפילין contain praise of ישראל, so he asks whether ה׳ really gains glory from ישראל's praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תפילין contain praise of ה׳, which makes sense because they glorify Him. ה׳'s תפילין contain praise of ישראל, and that sounds strange. Why would the Creator's 'glory' be bound up with a nation's praise? This question asks for the basis of that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (Aramaic form)

phrases.english: And is the Holy One, Blessed be He, glorified
phrases.notes: וּמִי here means 'is it really so?' It is not the word 'who'.

phrases.english: through the praises of Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מִשְׁתַּבַּח קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּשִׁבְחַיְיהוּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on step 28's claim that ה׳'s תפילין contain praise of ישראל
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a basis for saying ה׳ is glorified through ישראל's praise?

steps.title: Yes: you made Me unique, and I will make you unique
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין answers yes. Two matching פסוקים show a two-way relationship: ישראל made ה׳ one unique entity, and ה׳ makes ישראל one unique entity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as it is written: 'You have declared ה׳ today,' and it is written: 'And ה׳ has declared you today.' The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to ישראל: You made Me one unique entity in the world, and I will make you one unique entity in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין says yes. He brings two side-by-side פסוקים in which ישראל 'declares' ה׳ and ה׳ 'declares' ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים use the same word, הֶאֱמַרְתָּ and הֶאֱמִירְךָ, which shows a mutual relationship. Because ישראל singles ה׳ out as unique, ה׳ singles ישראל out as unique. That is why praise of ישראל belongs in ה׳'s תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: you have declared / singled out; He has declared / singled you out
one unique entity, singled out from everything else

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the theme of a mutual relationship: ישראל's תפילין praise ה׳, and ה׳'s 'תפילין' praise ישראל.

phrases.english: Yes, as it is written:
"You have affirmed the Lord this day."
phrases.notes: דברים כו:יז

phrases.english: And it is written: "And the Lord has affirmed you this day,"
phrases.notes: דברים כו:יח

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
You have made Me a single unique entity in the world,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אֶתְכֶם חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: and I will make you a single unique entity in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The paired פסוקים show a mutual singling-out between ה׳ and ישראל.

steps.title: The sources for each side of the mutual relationship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק for each half of the relationship: שמע ישראל shows how ישראל makes ה׳ unique, and ומי כעמך ישראל shows how ה׳ makes ישראל unique.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You made Me one unique entity in the world,' as it says: 'Hear, ישראל‎, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One.' 'And I will make you one unique entity in the world,' as it says: 'Who is like Your people ישראל, one nation in the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly where each half of the relationship appears in a פסוק. Each half gets its own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישראל declares ה׳'s oneness in קריאת שמע, and our תפילין contain that פרשה‎. ה׳ declares ישראל's uniqueness with 'גוי אחד', which is the very פסוק step 28 said is in ה׳'s תפילין. The word אחד links the two sides, so the picture fits together.

keyTerms.meaning: Hear, O Israel (the declaration of ה׳'s oneness)

steps.whatToRemember: Our תפילין say 'ה׳ is One' (שמע ישראל‎). ה׳'s תפילין say 'ישראל is one nation' (ומי כעמך ישראל). The relationship is mutual.

phrases.english: You have made Me a single unique entity in the world,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד״,
phrases.english: as it is stated: "Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One,"
phrases.notes: דברים ו:ד. This is in the תפילין of ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אֶתְכֶם חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם״,
phrases.english: and I will make you a single unique entity in the world,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וּמִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: "Who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א יז:כא. This is the פסוק from step 28.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתֶּם עֲשִׂיתוּנִי חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the specific פסוק behind each half of step 30's statement
steps.raayaObject: The mutual 'singling out' between ה׳ and ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמע ישראל (דברים ו:ד) and ומי כעמך ישראל (דברי הימים א יז:כא)

steps.title: What is in the other compartments?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי: that covers one compartment of ה׳'s תפילין של ראש. What is written in the remaining compartments?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: That works for one compartment. In the other compartments, what is written?
steps.whatsHappening: A new pair of אמוראים raises a follow-up. תפילין של ראש have four separate compartments, and so far we have only filled one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תפילין של ראש hold four different פרשיות in four compartments. If ה׳'s תפילין mirror ours, we need more praises of ישראל to fill the other compartments. The question asks for that missing content.

keyTerms.meaning: it works out well / that is fine
compartment / compartments (of the תפילין של ראש)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
It works out well for one compartment;
in the rest of the compartments, what is written?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בְּחַד בֵּיתָא, בִּשְׁאָר בָּתֵּי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that step 28's answer only fills one of the four compartments
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which praises of ישראל fill the other compartments of ה׳'s תפילין של ראש?

steps.title: רב אשי lists more verses praising Israel
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers with five more פסוקים praising ישראל that are written in the other compartments.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'For who is a great nation,' 'And who is a great nation,' 'Happy are you, ישראל,' 'Or has God attempted,' and 'And to place you supreme.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by naming the other praises of ישראל found in ה׳'s תפילין. Each one is a פסוק that describes ישראל's greatness or uniqueness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק praises ישראל‎: ה׳ is close to them, they have righteous laws, ה׳ saves them, ה׳ took them out with miracles, and ה׳ raises them above all nations. These parallel the praises of ה׳ in our תפילין.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי lists five פסוקים, but only three compartments are left to fill. Don't be thrown by that. The גמרא raises this exact problem in step 34 and solves it in step 35.

phrases.english: He (Rav Ashi) said to him:
"For who is a great nation"
phrases.notes: דברים ד:ז

phrases.english: "And who is a great nation"
phrases.notes: דברים ד:ח

phrases.english: "Happy are you, Israel"
phrases.notes: דברים לג:כט

phrases.english: "Or has God attempted"
phrases.notes: דברים ד:לד

phrases.english: "And to make you supreme"
phrases.notes: דברים כו:יט

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי מִי גוֹי גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The remaining compartments hold פסוקים praising ישראל: כי מי גוי גדול, ומי גוי גדול, אשריך ישראל, או הנסה אלהים, ולתתך עליון.

steps.title: Too many compartments for the head-תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא objects: if all these פסוקים are in ה׳'s תפילין של ראש, there are more passages than a head-תפילין has compartments.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there are too many compartments!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's list from the last step. Counting all the פסוקים, there would be more than the four compartments a תפילין של ראש has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תפילין של ראש always has exactly four compartments. One compartment already held the opening פסוק, and רב אשי then added five more פסוקים, one per compartment. That adds up to more than four, so the list as stated cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If all those פסוקים are in ה׳'s head-תפילין

phrases.english: there are too many compartments!
phrases.notes: A head-תפילין has only four compartments

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נְפִישִׁי לְהוּ טוּבֵי בָּתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the count in רב אשי's answer in Step 33
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's list giving each of the five פסוקים its own compartment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תפילין של ראש has only four compartments, but the list would need more than four.

steps.title: Similar פסוקים share a compartment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rearranges the פסוקים: the two 'great nation' פסוקים share one compartment, the two 'ישראל' praises share one, and the last two each get their own. That makes exactly four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'For who is a great nation' and 'And who is a great nation,' which are similar to each other, are in one compartment. 'Happy are you, ישראל' and 'Who is like Your people ישראל' are in one compartment. 'Or has God tried' is in one compartment. 'And to make you high' is in one compartment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pairing up פסוקים that sound alike. That way all the praises fit into exactly four compartments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every פסוק needs its own compartment. The two פסוקים beginning 'who is a great nation' match, so they go together. 'ומי כעמך ישראל' joins its look-alike 'אשריך ישראל'. Together with 'או הנסה' and 'ולתתך עליון', that is four compartments, just like a real תפילין של ראש.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a פסוק was removed. Every פסוק stays. The only change is that look-alike פסוקים now share a compartment, so the total comes to four.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳'s תפילין של ראש has four compartments, like ours: (1) כי מי גוי גדול and ומי גוי גדול, (2) אשריך ישראל and ומי כעמך ישראל, (3) או הנסה אלהים, (4) ולתתך עליון.

phrases.english: Rather: 'For who is a great nation'
phrases.notes: דברים ד:ז

phrases.english: and 'And who is a great nation,' which resemble each other,
phrases.notes: דברים ד:ח; same opening words

phrases.english: are in one compartment;
'Happy are you, Israel' and 'Who is like Your people Israel'
phrases.notes: Both praise ישראל by name

phrases.english: are in one compartment;
'Or has God tried' is in one compartment;
phrases.notes: דברים ד:לד

phrases.english: 'And to make you high' is in one compartment.
phrases.notes: דברים כו:יט

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כִּי מִי גוֹי גָּדוֹל וּמִי גּוֹי גָּדוֹל דְּדָמְיָין לַהֲדָדֵי בְּחַד בֵּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the compartment-count problem raised in Step 34
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reorganization: look-alike פסוקים are grouped together to reduce the number of compartments
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each פסוק was assumed to need its own compartment, which gave too many.
steps.terutzMaskana: Similar פסוקים share a compartment, so all the praises fit into exactly four compartments.
